title: Production Readiness and Reliability
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main terms of Production Readiness and Reliability.
Use or interpret an appropriate PostgreSQL example connected to backup verification.
Identify one edge case and select a safe way to verify the expected result.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on Production Readiness and Reliability. Its primary job is to help you test data integrity and migration behavior, plan deployment boundaries and document a production readiness review. The listed PDF subtopics define the coverage expected here; work through them in order and connect each one to an example, edge case and checkable result.
content.why_it_matters: This topic matters because PostgreSQL systems must preserve correct results as data grows and more sessions or services interact with it. Practicing production readiness and reliability teaches you to make assumptions explicit, apply the right SQL or operational tool, and verify behavior instead of relying on a demonstration that only worked once.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep the problem small: test data integrity and migration behavior, plan deployment boundaries and document a production readiness review. A PostgreSQL feature should be chosen for the semantics it provides, not just because it is available. Before executing a change, state the inputs, expected output and boundary conditions. The example below is intentionally small enough to inspect; it illustrates the idea but is not a substitute for a test against your schema and PostgreSQL version.

items.title: Backup verification
items.text: Write down the recovery objective and confirm it by restoring into an isolated target; a successful dump alone is not a restore test.

items.title: Monitoring and alerting
items.text: Capture the time, database, role and exact diagnostic; separate the original failure from symptoms before changing settings.

items.title: Connection and storage capacity
items.text: Relate this point to production readiness and reliability: define the expected behavior, one edge case, and a query or check that would provide evidence.

items.title: Security review
items.text: Relate this point to production readiness and reliability: define the expected behavior, one edge case, and a query or check that would provide evidence.

items.title: Recovery drills and incident procedures
items.text: Write down the recovery objective and confirm it by restoring into an isolated target; a successful dump alone is not a restore test.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Production Readiness and Reliability
content_blocks.code: SELECT current_setting('server_version') AS server_version, current_database() AS database_name, current_user AS role_name;
content_blocks.expected_output: Returns basic runtime context as a starting point for a readiness checklist; it does not by itself establish production readiness.
content_blocks.safety_note: Read-only query; redact context details before sharing.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run with a normal least-privilege role, then complete the lesson checklist for backups, security, monitoring, migrations and recovery.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For a read-only SELECT or inspection command, no reset is needed. For DDL/DML, use a disposable database; capture the starting state, run the example, inspect the result, and ROLLBACK or drop the lab objects as appropriate. Do not use production data or credentials.

Treat the sample as inspectable code unless you run it yourself in an approved isolated environment. Python examples require a separate isolated runner.
content_blocks.schema_assumptions: Run with a normal least-privilege role, then complete the lesson checklist for backups, security, monitoring, migrations and recovery.

content_blocks.title: Practical checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Safety checkpoint: use least-privilege credentials, synthetic data, and a separate test database; verify results before applying a change to a real workload.

task: Create a short practice artifact for “Production Readiness and Reliability”: explain its goal, show one example linked to “Backup verification”, state the expected result, and include one edge/failure case and verification method. Use a disposable database or static artifact as appropriate.
hints: Start with the listed subtopics, especially “Backup verification”, and describe the expected behavior in your own words.
Run or inspect the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior; do not add unrelated features before it is verified.
When the result surprises you, capture the exact SQL/error, check version and permissions, and change one assumption at a time.
expected_output: A reviewable note or query for Production Readiness and Reliability, with an explanation of “Backup verification”, expected behavior, and a documented edge-case check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying the example without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Object names, data types, privileges, extensions and data distribution affect database behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: List schema/version assumptions and test with a tiny synthetic dataset first.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a single successful query as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: A happy-path result does not test invalid input, concurrent sessions, permissions, recovery or query performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one negative/edge case and record the evidence that confirms the expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Making a production change directly from a lesson.
common_mistakes.why: DDL, data updates, role changes and operational commands can affect data or availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use an isolated lab, reviewed migration, least privilege, rollback/recovery plan and a second-person review for production.

summary: Production Readiness and Reliability fits into the broader goal to test data integrity and migration behavior, plan deployment boundaries and document a production readiness review.
Use the curriculum subtopics as a completeness checklist: Backup verification, Monitoring and alerting, Connection and storage capacity.
State the schema/version assumptions and verify one normal case plus an edge case before trusting the result.
